units.label: Tactical Roadmap
units.text:
# Tactical Roadmap

The phased twelve-month sequence of the approved platform: signature moments balanced against an always-on presence, every tactic an Activation Card placed by date, channel, audience, message, phase and KPI (key performance indicator).

**The platform is approved: The Stop Line, decided by Kamen Kamenov.**
**The owners and the calendar below are not yet approved; no owner is recorded.**

**Period and markets.** The campaign period runs for 12 months through 30 June 2027 across the United States, the European Union and Sofia-relevant talent activity.

units.label: The phases
units.text:
## The phases

| phase | objective | months |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pre-Seed | Prepare The Stop Line proof base, approval route, public identity and message evidence before the AI (artificial intelligence) story is promoted. | 1 · 2 · 3 |
| Launch | Introduce The Stop Line through Signed by Humans and direct owners, buyers, partners and talent to approved proof. | 4 · 5 |
| Sustain | Keep The Stop Line visible through proof, explanation, senior craft and partner enablement between hero moments. | 6 · 7 · 8 · 9 |
| Amplify | Extend The Stop Line with third-party validation, advocacy and measurement without widening the AI claim. | 10 · 11 · 12 |

The four phases are the year. Inside a phase, each major moment runs Tease → Launch → Sustain → Amplify; across the year the corporate rollout widens the audience Engage → Enhance → Advocate → Amplify.

units.label: The Hero / Hub / Hygiene balance
units.text:
## The Hero / Hub / Hygiene balance

**Hero — signature moments, about a fifth.** Hero effort is carried by The Stop Line proof page, the Signed by Humans founder launch post and earned validation outreach, giving the year a few signature moments rather than constant launches.

**Hub — sustained programmes, about three fifths.** Hub effort is carried by owner testing, partner proof, technical proof, senior craft and employee advocacy, which sustain roughly three fifths of the programme through repeatable proof-led material.

**Hygiene — always-on maintenance, about a fifth.** Hygiene effort is carried by Conversation Management, the Observatory newsroom and the Month 12 scorecard, keeping the platform maintained, listened to and corrected between visible moments.

units.label: The Activation Cards
units.text:
## The Activation Cards

No tactic goes on the calendar until it is a card.

units.label: The Stop Line proof page
units.text:
### The Stop Line proof page

**Insight.** Buyers do not need a bigger AI promise; they need to see what is proved, who owns it and where the system stops.

**Idea.** Create one owned page that introduces The Stop Line and shows each approved claim with its proof type, senior owner and stated limit; live, unpromoted, until the Launch moment in Month 4.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Visitors can inspect the proof behind each claim before they are asked to book a meeting or accept the AI story.

**Desired outcome.** The B Team has a public proof base that paid, earned, shared and sales activity can all point to.  ·  **Targets.** Read in Month 2 for claim completeness, proof-label completion and approval-route readiness before public promotion in Month 4.  ·  **Approver.** Kamen Kamenov

**Signature.** The Stop Line  ·  **KPI.** Approved public AI claims linked to proof — percentage, The Stop Line proof-link register · Qualified meeting clicks from proof page — count, Owned proof-page analytics report · Proof-page inspection depth — count, Proof-page section engagement report  ·  **Months.** 2 to 12

units.label: Owner control message test
units.text:
### Owner control message test

**Insight.** Elena's preference for control and visibility is a strong hypothesis, but it is not settled buyer truth until owners compare the messages.

**Idea.** Test a control-led message against an AI-capability message, both anchored in The Stop Line.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Owners react to plain-language options that show visibility, ownership and early risk detection without asking them to become technical buyers.

**Desired outcome.** The B Team learns whether control should lead owner-facing communication before scaling the message.  ·  **Targets.** In Month 3, read the Launch message with the owner and get their written confirmation that it reflects their preference, is easy to understand, builds trust and supports the meeting’s purpose before it is sent.  ·  **Approver.** Kamen Kamenov

**Signature.** Restraint is the proof.  ·  **KPI.** Owner message preference — percentage, Owner message-test preference report · Plain-language comprehension — 1-5 score, Owner comprehension rubric · Meeting intent after message exposure — percentage, Owner test intent register  ·  **Month.** 3

units.label: Conversation Management loop and Observatory newsroom
units.text:
### Conversation Management loop and Observatory newsroom

**Insight.** Campaign moments cannot hold a reputation if the market is already asking trust, governance and AI-risk questions every day.

**Idea.** Run the always-on listening, triage, response and escalation loop for The Stop Line so the team enters only moments where approved proof and a visible limit exist.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Questions, issues and market hooks are logged, matched to approved answers and escalated when the proof boundary is missing.

**Desired outcome.** The B Team responds consistently between campaigns and does not widen the AI story under pressure.  ·  **Targets.** Always-on from Month 1 through Month 12, read weekly for response readiness, approved-answer reuse and unresolved escalation themes.  ·  **Approver.** Kamen Kamenov

**Signature.** Proof before promotion  ·  **KPI.** Approved-answer reuse — count, Conversation Management response register · Escalated unresolved proof gaps — count, Observatory escalation log · Message consistency in live responses — 1-5 score, Weekly response-quality checklist  ·  **Months.** 1 to 12

units.label: Signed by Humans founder launch post
units.text:
### Signed by Humans founder launch post

**Insight.** The human moment makes the AI story credible when a senior person visibly checks, owns and signs the work.

**Idea.** Publish a founder-led launch post that explains Signed by Humans as the visible promise behind The Stop Line.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Readers see the senior responsibility behind the claim and are directed to the owned proof page for evidence.

**Desired outcome.** Founder visibility increases while the public story stays inside the approved proof boundary.  ·  **Targets.** Read in Month 5 for founder-post reach, proof-page clicks, partner reshares and qualified inbound conversations after the Month 4 proof launch.  ·  **Approver.** Kamen Kamenov

**Signature.** Signed by Humans  ·  **KPI.** Proof-page clicks from founder post — count, Founder launch post analytics report · Engagement quality — 1-5 score, Founder-post engagement-quality rubric · Qualified inbound conversations — count, Founder visibility inbound register  ·  **Month.** 5

units.label: Partner proof pack
units.text:
### Partner proof pack

**Insight.** Referral partners can carry the story only if the approved proof is simple, repeatable and safe to share.

**Idea.** Build a short partner pack that explains The Stop Line, Signed by Humans and the approved proof types behind each claim.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Partners get language they can use without inventing claims or stretching evidence.

**Desired outcome.** Referral conversations become easier, more consistent and less exposed to unapproved AI claims.  ·  **Targets.** Read in Month 6 for partner briefing completion, pack use and claim-compliance before earned outreach widens.  ·  **Approver.** Kamen Kamenov

**Signature.** Proof before promotion  ·  **KPI.** Partner briefings completed — count, Partner proof briefing register · Partner pack use in referrals — count, Partner pack usage log · Claim-compliant partner language — percentage, Partner claim-compliance checklist  ·  **Months.** 6 to 10

units.label: Technical proof story
units.text:
### Technical proof story

**Insight.** Technical buyers need evidence that AI supports delivery without taking ownership away from senior people.

**Idea.** Publish a technical proof story under The Stop Line showing the claim, proof type, senior owner and stated limit behind an AI-supported delivery example.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Technical buyers inspect the artifact and see what is confirmed, what is not claimed and who signs the boundary.

**Desired outcome.** Technical trust grows without turning The Stop Line into an unbounded AI capability pitch.  ·  **Targets.** Read in Month 7 for artifact views, sales use and qualified technical conversations.  ·  **Approver.** Matthew Maday

**Signature.** The Stop Line  ·  **KPI.** Technical artifact views — count, Technical artifact analytics report · Sales use of technical proof — count, Sales proof-use register · Qualified technical conversations — count, Technical buyer conversation log  ·  **Months.** 7 to 12

units.label: Senior craft story series
units.text:
### Senior craft story series

**Insight.** Senior Sofia talent and careful buyers will believe the AI story only if it protects judgment rather than celebrating automation alone.

**Idea.** Publish a recurring always-on-after-launch series under Signed by Humans that shows how senior people review work, make decisions and define the stop line.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Readers see craft, judgment and responsibility inside AI-supported delivery.

**Desired outcome.** The talent story and buyer story reinforce each other without turning The B Team into a broad ethics platform.  ·  **Targets.** Monthly from Month 6 through Month 12, read after each story for senior-talent engagement, buyer engagement and proof-page clicks.  ·  **Approver.** Kamen Kamenov

**Signature.** Signed by Humans  ·  **KPI.** Senior-talent engagement — count, Senior craft story engagement report · Qualified candidate interest — count, Talent interest register · Buyer proof-page clicks from craft stories — count, Craft story clickthrough report  ·  **Months.** 6 to 12

units.label: Earned validation outreach
units.text:
### Earned validation outreach

**Insight.** The Stop Line becomes harder to dismiss when credible third parties can inspect the proof instead of repeating a company claim.

**Idea.** Brief journalists, analysts and named experts on The Stop Line only after the proof page, partner pack and technical proof story exist.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Professional influencers receive the approved fact sheet, proof citations and claim limits before any interview or story pitch.

**Desired outcome.** Third-party credibility extends the platform without widening the AI claim.  ·  **Targets.** From Month 10 through Month 12, read monthly for briefings secured, proof citations and coverage quality.  ·  **Approver.** Kamen Kamenov

**Signature.** The Stop Line  ·  **KPI.** Proof-led briefings secured — count, Earned outreach briefing register · Coverage quality — 1-5 score, Earned coverage-quality rubric · Published proof citations — count, Proof citation tracker  ·  **Months.** 10 to 12

units.label: Employee advocacy enablement
units.text:
### Employee advocacy enablement

**Insight.** Employees can only advocate for The Stop Line if they have approved language, proof links and clear limits.

**Idea.** Equip the advocates trained by the Conversation Management loop with Signed by Humans posts, proof links and do-not-say guardrails.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Employees choose approved proof-led prompts and share only claims already connected to The Stop Line.

**Desired outcome.** Employee advocacy increases visibility while staying inside the approved claim boundary.  ·  **Targets.** Read in Month 11 for employee participation, post quality and proof-page clicks after Conversation Management has trained the response pattern from Month 1.  ·  **Approver.** Kamen Kamenov

**Signature.** Signed by Humans  ·  **KPI.** Employee participation — count, Employee advocacy participation register · Advocacy post quality — 1-5 score, Employee advocacy quality rubric · Proof-page clicks from employee posts — count, Employee advocacy analytics report  ·  **Month.** 11

units.label: Close scorecard and message recalibration
units.text:
### Close scorecard and message recalibration

**Insight.** A proof-first platform must close the year by showing what was proved, what changed and what proof gaps remain.

**Idea.** Produce a Month 12 executive scorecard for The Stop Line and recalibrate the Key-Message Table without expanding the AI claim.

**Engagement — the mechanic.** Owners review the scorecard, approve message changes and name next-year proof gaps before the next cycle starts.

**Desired outcome.** The next year begins from measured proof, not from campaign memory or unapproved ambition.  ·  **Targets.** Read in Month 12 for scorecard completion, approved message changes and named proof gaps.  ·  **Approver.** Kamen Kamenov

**Signature.** The Stop Line  ·  **KPI.** Executive scorecard completion — percentage, Month 12 executive scorecard checklist · Approved message changes — count, Key-Message Table change register · Named next-year proof gaps — count, Proof gap register  ·  **Month.** 12

units.label: The always-on loop
units.text:
## The always-on loop

Underneath the phases runs the Conversation Management loop — supported by the always-on newsroom running proactive stories and reactive issues management: establish goals → gather assets → develop proprietary content → deploy across owned, earned and paid → train advocates → deploy the trained advocates → measure → refine. The advocates are employees and senior advocates trained through the Conversation Management loop, equipped by Employee advocacy enablement in Month 11; they deploy from Month 11, and until then the loop runs its other steps without them.

units.label: The proof-building order
units.text:
## The proof-building order

**Cases first** — Months 1 to 12: Conversation Management loop and Observatory newsroom, The Stop Line proof page, Owner control message test, Partner proof pack, Technical proof story. This stage proves The Stop Line has approved proof, buyer-tested language, partner-safe claims and technical evidence before the story is widened.

**Thought leadership second** — Months 5 to 12: Signed by Humans founder launch post, Senior craft story series. This stage proves the platform can be explained through senior responsibility and craft without becoming a broad AI promise.

**Visibility third** — Months 10 to 12: Earned validation outreach, Employee advocacy enablement, Close scorecard and message recalibration. This stage proves The Stop Line can travel through third parties, employees and executive review while staying inside approved proof and visible limits.

units.label: The rollout
units.text:
## The rollout

**First audience.** Owners of midsize businesses who want control and visibility, represented by Elena.

**Then widen — from Month 5 to Month 12.** After the owner message is tested and the proof page is public, the platform widens to technical buyers, partners, senior Sofia talent, professional influencers and employees using the same proof-first story.

units.label: Global to local
units.text:
## Global to local

The global core is one channel-agnostic set of beats: The Stop Line, Signed by Humans, proof before promotion, senior responsibility and visible limits; local markets adapt hooks, language, spokespeople and local proof while keeping the platform, narrative, do-not-say lines and global KPIs fixed, with local targets set for proof-link percentage, trust lift, qualified conversations, proof citations and claim-compliance rate.

units.label: Client Style Note applied
units.text:
## Client Style Note applied

- **tone:** The client's owned voice is concise, technical and aspirational, with a craft-and-AI contrast at its center.
- **sentence length:** Sentences are mostly short to medium, with one clear claim per line or paragraph.
- **vocabulary:** The vocabulary combines engineering terms with human delivery language: AI development, enterprise-grade software, automation, architect-led delivery, craft, workflow and fit.
- **self reference:** The client refers to itself as The B Team and uses first-person plural sparingly through service and contact language.
- **signature do words:** AI, craftsmanship, enterprise-grade, architect-led, hand-crafted, agentic AI, workflow automations, fit
- **signature dont words:** cheap offshore, best-in-class, game-changing, world-class, revolutionary, full-service agency, marketing activation
- **sources:** https://thebteam.com/, https://thebteam.com/about, https://thebteam.com/services, https://thebteam.com/process, https://thebteam.com/case-studies, https://thebteam.com/privacy-policy
- **long form voice:** Not yet calibrated: no long-form writing of the client's own has been read.
- **claim boundary:** These are the client's own published words; every claim they carry stays inside the approved proof and the do-not-say lines, and none of them widens what the platform allows this page to say.
